name: Insight-HXMT
summary: Chinese hard-X-ray astronomy satellite whose observations have been used to constrain dark-matter abundance through primordial-black-hole Hawking radiation.
detection_principle: Collimated detectors in different energy bands measure X-ray intensities and spectra, comparing diffuse radiation and background models with PBH-evaporation predictions.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: NASA's current mission page lists 2017 to the present but gives no independent status date.

collaboration.name: Insight-HXMT collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Institutional participation refers to the period covered by each source; this dossier does not claim to provide a complete membership list.

key_parameters.name: LE / ME / HE energy bands
key_parameters.value: 1–12 / 5–30 / 20–350 keV, nominal values in NASA's overview

key_parameters.name: Representative PBH study range
key_parameters.value: 10^16–10^18 g; conclusions depend on background models

results.summary: External data reanalysis constrains PBH abundance; not direct particle detection by the collaboration.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
